plan.title: Separate contributor onboarding from the general user flow (don't gate everyone on a "are you working on deft itself?" question)

narratives.Description: Separate contributor onboarding from the general user flow (don't gate everyone on a "are you working on deft itself?" question). This story closes the linked GitHub issue with a scoped fix, tests, and a CHANGELOG entry. File scope and verify commands are recorded under plan.metadata.swarm for concurrent allocation.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

When a user starts Directive via `QUICK-START.md`, the very first step asks **"Are you (1) using deft in your project, or (2) working on deft itself?"** This front-loads a contributor-only branch onto every user. The overwhelming majority are option (1) — they just want to use Deft — so we're taxing the common path to serve a small subset. We should separate internal contributor onboarding from the general flow rather than gating everyone on it.

## Current behavior

`QUICK-START.md` Step 1 (the entry point for manual clones and for stale-AGENTS.md / redirect-stub routing) opens with:

> Ask the user: **"Are you (1) using deft in your project, or (2) working on deft itself?"**
> - If **(2)**: ... read `./AGENTS.md` ... **Stop here.**
> - If **(1)**: Continue to Step 2.

So the first interaction every QUICK-START user has is a fork that 99% of them answer "(1)" to before any real setup begins.

## Why this is the wrong default

- **It's invasive for the majority.** Consumers installing Deft to use it never need the contributor branch, yet they must answer it first, every time.
- **The contributor branch is largely redundant.** A genuine framework contributor working inside a `deftai/directive` checkout already has the repo's own contributor `AGENTS.md` and uses the `--maintainer` installer flag (`cmd/deft-install`). They don't rely on QUICK-START Step 1 to be routed.
- **The binary-installer happy path already does the right thing.** The installer writes `AGENTS.md` from `templates/agents-entry.md`, whose managed section goes straight to the First Session / `USER.md` flow with no contributor question. Only the QUICK-START entry point (manual clone + upgrade routing) carries the fork, so the experience is already inconsistent between entry paths.

## Proposal

Make the general user flow the default and move contributor onboarding out of the gating position.

**Recommended (non-blocking pointer):**
- Remove the up-front "(1) or (2)" gate from `QUICK-START.md` Step 1; default straight into the consumer flow (Step 2 — Detect project state).
- Add a single, non-blocking pointer for contributors — either at the *end* of QUICK-START or in the README/CONTRIBUTING — e.g. "Working on Deft itself? See `CONTRIBUTING.md` and use the `--maintainer` install path." It informs without interrupting.

**Alternative (cleaner, slightly more aggressive):**
- Drop the contributor fork from QUICK-START entirely. Contributors are already served by the repo's own `AGENTS.md` and `--maintainer`; QUICK-START is a consumer-facing artifact and doesn't need a contributor branch at all.

## Scope / where it lands

- `QUICK-START.md` — remove/relocate the Step 1 fork; renumber subsequent steps.
- `README.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` — ensure the contributor entry point is clearly documented in a place contributors actually look (so removing the fork loses no information).
- Check `templates/agents-entry.md` and `docs/getting-started.md` for any matching language so the consumer-vs-contributor split is described consistently across entry points.

## Open questions

1. Remove the fork entirely, or keep a non-blocking end-of-flow pointer? (Draft recommends the pointer.)
2. Does any automation, test, or doc currently depend on QUICK-START Step 1's numbering or its contributor branch? (`tests/content/` references QUICK-START in places — verify nothing asserts the fork before removing it.)
3. Should the contributor path get its own short `CONTRIBUTING`-anchored quickstart so "working on deft itself" has a real home rather than just "read AGENTS.md"?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user following `QUICK-START.md` is no longer asked a contributor-vs-user question before setup begins; the consumer flow is the default.
- [ ] Contributors retain a clear, documented entry point (CONTRIBUTING / `--maintainer`)
      — no information is lost, it's just moved out of the gating position.
- [ ] QUICK-START step numbering and any cross-references remain consistent after the change.
- [ ] Existing QUICK-START content tests pass (or are updated to reflect the new flow).

---

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-06-21T19:20:27Z)

Scoping note after checking current `HEAD`: the consumer-vs-contributor distinction is **already auto-detected** in two places, so this issue is narrower than the title suggests.

1. **Runtime code already distinguishes it** — `scripts/_project_context.py::is_framework_source_context()` compares `framework_root == project_root` (vendored `.deft/core` vs. a source checkout) and routes `check:framework-source` vs. `check:consumer` with no human prompt.
2. **The binary-installer happy path never asks** — it writes `AGENTS.md` from `templates/agents-entry.md` straight into the consumer first-session flow.

The "(1) using deft / (2) working on deft itself?" fork survives in exactly one place: `QUICK-START.md` Step 1, which is reached only via a manual clone or stale-AGENTS.md / redirect-stub upgrade routing. QUICK-START's Step 2 already does deterministic filesystem detection immediately after, so the same context could be inferred rather than asked.

**Net:** the premise that "we tax *every* user" is overstated — the installer path and runtime code already auto-detect; only the manual-clone / upgrade-routing entry still asks. Scope is just removing/relocating the QUICK-START Step 1 leftover (the issue's "Alternative"), not a broad UX fix.
narratives.UserStory: As a new Directive user, I want onboarding to assume I am a consumer by default, so that I am not gated on a contributor-only question.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Edit QUICK-START.md and content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md so the default path is consumer project use. 2. Move the contributor / working-on-deft-itself branch behind an explicit secondary prompt. 3. Add or update content-contract tests under packages/core/src/content-contracts if present. 4. Verify with rg on the skill file and vitest content contracts; CHANGELOG Closes #1813.
